# Jubilees Chapter 40 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Joseph's exaltation; the famine; the brothers come to Egypt

---

**40:1** In the first year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee, Pharaoh dreamed two dreams in the same night, and he was troubled by both of them.

**40:2** Joseph was brought before Pharaoh and interpreted his two dreams. It was established that there would be seven years of abundance throughout all the land of Egypt, followed by seven years of famine.

**40:3** Pharaoh appointed Joseph over all his land and made him ruler over all Egypt. Pharaoh said to him: "No one shall be greater than you in all the land of Egypt except me."

**40:4** Pharaoh gave Joseph the name Zaphenath-paneah and gave him Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of Heliopolis, as his wife.

**40:5** Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh. He went out from Pharaoh's presence and traveled through all the land of Egypt.

**40:6** In the seven years of abundance, Joseph gathered all the food of the land and stored it in the cities. Then the seven years of famine began, after the years of abundance.

**40:7** Famine was throughout all the land except Egypt. Joseph opened all the storehouses and sold grain to the Egyptians and to all the peoples of the earth.

**40:8** The sons of Jacob came to Egypt to buy grain, for the famine was severe in the land of Canaan as well.

**40:9** Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him. He spoke harshly to them and questioned them about their father and about their younger brother Benjamin.

**40:10** They said: "Our father is alive and our younger brother is with him." Joseph bound Simeon and told them to bring Benjamin.

**40:11** They returned to the land of Canaan and told their father Jacob everything that had happened to them.

**40:12** Jacob said: "You have bereaved me: Joseph is gone, and Simeon is gone, and now you want to take Benjamin." He refused to send Benjamin.

**40:13** Reuben said: "Put my two sons to death if I do not bring him back to you." But Jacob would not send Benjamin with Reuben.

**40:14** Then Judah said to Jacob: "Send the boy with me; I will be surety for him." Jacob consented and sent Benjamin with his brothers.

**40:15** They came before Joseph. Joseph saw his brother Benjamin and wept. He went into a chamber and wept there. Then he washed his face, came out, and restrained himself.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus following LOGOS. The Asenath marriage (v.4) is noted without the extended commentary found in later texts (e.g., the Joseph and Asenath novella). Judah's suretyship for Benjamin (v.14) marks his leadership role, consistent with the Shiloh oracle of ch.38.*
